name: Bou Inania Madrasa
hero_subtitle: A Marinid masterpiece of zellige, carved stucco and cedar on Talaa Kebira.

overview.title: A Religious School Open to Everyone
overview.p1: Bou Inania Madrasa was built in the mid-14th century under the Marinid sultan Abu Inan Faris and is considered one of the finest examples of Marinid architecture. It is one of the few religious buildings in Fes that non-Muslim visitors can enter, which makes it especially worth a stop.
overview.p2: The central courtyard is the highlight: a marble-paved space with a central fountain, walls layered with zellige mosaics, carved stucco and cedar woodwork. Upstairs, small student cells look down on the court. Visit early for a quieter courtyard, and look out for the Dar al-Magana water clock across the lane.

moods.title: What to See at Bou Inania
moods.subtitle: Small, dense and beautiful.

1.title: The Central Courtyard
1.desc: Marble paving, a fountain and walls layered with tile, stucco and cedar. Stand still and look up.

2.title: Student Cells & Gallery
2.desc: Small upstairs rooms show how students once lived and studied, looking onto the court.

3.title: The Water Clock Across the Lane
3.desc: Dar al-Magana's row of bronze bowls and wooden brackets is a curiosity worth a look from the street.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Bou Inania Madrasa

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: It is on Talaa Kebira, about 10 minutes from Bab Bou Jeloud. Walk down the main lane and you'll reach it.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Usually open in the daytime with hours that vary. Arrive early for a quieter courtyard, and check current hours and price.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: The prayer hall itself is closed to non-Muslim visitors. Dress modestly and respect the quiet of the space.

q1.question: Can non-Muslims visit Bou Inania Madrasa?
q1.answer: Yes. It is one of the few religious buildings in Fes open to non-Muslims, apart from the prayer hall.

q2.question: How long do you need at Bou Inania?
q2.answer: About 30 to 45 minutes is enough for the courtyard, the upper cells and the details.

q3.question: Is there an entrance fee?
q3.answer: Yes, admission is charged. Check the current rate and hours locally.

q4.question: What is the best time to visit?
q4.answer: Early in the day, when the courtyard is quieter and the light is good.
